plot: On the first frost night the Dough Bros cross the icy garden to the front fence to see who is inside Walter's bakery, closed for fifty years; Lolly slides into the leaves, the porch light freezes them, Zeek's glasses-telescope fogs until he wipes it on Bup's crust, and the 'burglar' turns out to be old Walter himself, sweeping and setting two cups out with a sign for Rosie; scared Pim climbs the feeder pole and shakes the wind chime so Grandma wakes and runs over — then the radio warns of an all-day power cut tomorrow, with the Thanksgiving turkey in the freezer.

script.title: First Frost: Who's in the Closed Bakery?

beats.say: A light! In Walter's bakery! It's been dark for fifty years!
Then who walks into a dead bakery at midnight? A burglar?
Midnight. The first frost of November. The whole house is asleep.
Across Maple Street, one yellow window glows in the old bakery.
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
From the kitchen we see nothing. We need the front fence.
The fence? That's the whole frozen garden away!
Then we cross it. Quietly. Frost cracks like glass.
The Dough Bros slip out under the kitchen door into the cold.
Zeek drags a paper towel tube behind him through the grass.
My telescope. Two lenses from my old glasses. Pure genius.
Lolly steps onto one frosty leaf. And she keeps on going.
Wheee! No! No no no! I can't stop! Somebody grab me!
She slides across the whole lawn, straight into a pile of leaves.
I'm fine. I meant to do that. Nobody laugh. Nobody.
Halfway across, a small sensor on the porch blinks red.
Click. The porch light floods the whole garden white.
Nobody move. That light only sees things that move.
I c-can't stop shaking! I'm a bean! Beans shake!
Then shake behind me, Pim. I'm the darkest thing out here.
If that light wakes Dad, we never find out who's inside!
They reach the front fence. Frost sparkles on every bar.
The cold fogs both lenses. Everything goes milky white.
Fog! My genius telescope is now a genius cloud!
Wipe it on my crust. Stale bread is great for wiping.
Zeek rubs the lens on Bup's crust. Squeak. Squeak. Squeak.
Just so you know, that is my face.
Clear glass at last. The bakery window jumps up close.
A man. Very old. A long brown coat. A wooden cane.
A s-slow burglar? Those are the worst. They never leave.
Then we warn the house. The wind chime! Somebody ring it!
The chime hangs on the bird feeder pole. High above them.
Bup, wait! Look at what he's doing first.
The old man isn't grabbing anything. He's sweeping the floor.
Then he sets two cups on the windowsill. Not one. Two.
Burglars don't sweep. And they don't bring an extra cup.
He's taping a paper to the glass. Big letters. Reading.
Shaky letters: ROSIE. THE DOOR IS OPEN. W.
W? Walter! The baker! He came back for her!
And Grandma's asleep! If she misses tonight, it could be too late!
The chime. Somebody has to climb that icy feeder pole.
Slowly, everyone looks at the smallest, shakiest bro.
M-me? I shake. I shake all the time. At everything.
Exactly, Pim. Tonight, shaking is the whole job.
Pim climbs the icy pole. His legs tremble the whole way up.
At the top he wraps himself around the chime. And shakes.
Ting-a-ling-a-ling! The loudest chime on all of Maple Street.
Upstairs, Grandma's window lights up. A face. A gasp.
A minute later: slippers, a coat, and a little gold key.
I d-did it! My shaking finally helped somebody!
Across the street, two old friends hug in the yellow window.
Fifty years. And one tiny bean rang the bell.
Back inside, Dad's forgotten radio crackles on the counter.
Storm warning. Power cut tomorrow on Maple Street. All day long.
No power means no freezer. And the Thanksgiving turkey's in there!
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.

"난 뭐든지 무서워서 떨어. 오늘 밤엔 그게 드디어 쓸모 있었어." — 핌
